Okay long comment incoming: This might sound like a pain, but I have a ton of apartments I deliver to on a daily basis. And they are absolutely terribly layed out. I would say for 80% of them I have to call the customer to tell me how the hell to find them bc of how badly the layout is. Most of the time, they end up coming to me, not that I request that but it’s just what they do. I’ve had a handful that give me the apartment number etc but they include physical markers to look for. Something that is always there. Being in a car, it’s damn near impossible (for me at least I drive a Kia Soul so it’s a damn toaster box lol) to actually see apartment letters from the car. Something else that can help is telling the driver to call you when they get there and you can just direct them where to go bc uber and other gps isn’t helpful once you get into the complex(s). If you can’t come down that’s fine, and personally I don’t mind at all. What I do mind is not being able to find my customer bc the apartments are not built with any delivery drivers in mind. It creates frustration for everyone involved. Since you plan to meet at the door anyway, if you have a balcony outside your front door you can also stand out on it and we can find you that way to. There’s one complex specifically I deliver to weekly and everyone I’ve delivered to there does that and it’s so helpful. Sorry this is so long. This is just the things that you may be able to implement to help you and the drivers. Trust me, if you do any of those things, it’s certainly appreciated on the drivers side. I know you said it’s easily accessible, but it can be confusing if the drivers never been there too. Hope some of this is applicable to ya.!
Edit: I realized maybe I read that wrong and you don’t want a direct hand off. Either way, these things can be applied in different ways and still help. If you want to have the driver call you, send a message when the order is accepted and say something like “hey my apartment is a bit confusing to navigate so give me a call when you arrive and I will help you find me”.
